items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: You know John Coltrane, I mean we all got a chance to watch that develop you know, from the beginning when he put that quartet together

ctx.x: I wondered on occasion if the musicians like yourself and the fellas you mentioned sat around and talked about how they were going to play. Was there discussions that said like we might say, all right, we’re not going to play in this particular time signature, we’re just going to see what happens? Or I guess what I’m trying to say was any of this music pre-planned before you got on the bandstand or did it happen as it was being created?

I would imagine some of it did happen as it was being created, that whoever was the band leader said, you know, this is, you know, these couple of notes or whatever, maybe. Let’s just work off of that and, you know, see what we get. You know John Coltrane, I mean we all got a chance to watch that develop you know, from the beginning when he put that quartet together, finally, who were going to be in it for that run ‘til his death. And they rehearsed you know. And when it got to the point when he decided he wanted…

items.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I mean John Coltrane, he experimented with not playing in the minor you know, towards the end of his life you know.

ctx.x: That’s always the hardest part for me is the chord changes, finding something that’s interesting but — you had said, I really got a kick out of your story about learning about the minor nine chord in college, because I had the same experience except it was with the major seven. And for a while it was all about major sevenths. And eventually it got a little bit too happy for me so I had to —

Well you know sometimes it’s a lot more difficult to get some sort of solo activity out of major rather than minor. And as you probably know, I mean John Coltrane, he experimented with not playing in the minor you know, towards the end of his life you know. He did a lot of things off of a major feeling as opposed to a minor feeling.

I’ve been reading a little bit about Sun Ra and that — I guess very experimental music that he did and others at that time. I wonder if you had any experience hearing him or groups like the Art Ensemble of Chicago, that were — I mean they were out there I guess is the best way I can put it. And I’m wondering if you’d ever heard them live?
